Class PagedGridModel<T>

java.lang.Object
de.schladebeck.fx.grid.model.AbstractGridModel
de.schladebeck.fx.grid.model.PagedGridModel<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the type of the items
All Implemented Interfaces:
GridModel
public class PagedGridModel<T> extends AbstractGridModel

A model for data that is too large or too slow to load at once, such as a database table or a remote service. Rows are loaded page by page on a background thread when the grid first shows them:

PagedGridModel<Person> people = new PagedGridModel<Person>(repository.count(),
        page -> repository.find(page.offset(), page.count(), page.sortColumns()))
        .column("Name", Person::name)
        .column("City", Person::city);
Grid grid = new Grid(people);
  • Cells of rows that are still loading are empty (null) and fill in when their page arrives. Only the rows on screen are repainted then.
  • Pages are loaded newest request first, at most 4 at a time, so fast scrolling loads what is on screen now. Requests waiting beyond 16 are dropped, oldest first. A loader call that never returns keeps one of the 4 slots busy until the next reload or sort.
  • The 64 most recently used pages stay in memory, more while the grid shows more pages at once.
  • Clicking a column header sorts at the source: the grid calls sortRows(List, IntFunction), the cache is dropped and the loader gets the new order in its PagedGridModel.PageRequest, one or more columns. The grid never reads all rows to sort them.
  • Filtering belongs to the source as well: change what the loader queries and call reload(int) with the new row count. Grid row filters would read every row and should not be used with this model.
  • Columns are read-only; edit in a form and write to the source, then reload().

      public void setOnLoadError(Consumer<Throwable> handler)

    • sortRows

      public boolean sortRows(List<SortKey> keys, IntFunction<Comparator<Object>> order)
      Sorts at the source: drops the loaded pages and lets the loader load in the new order.
      Parameters:
      keys - the columns to sort by, the first one decides and the next ones break its ties; empty for the model's natural order
      order - the order of a model column's values, ascending, nulls first: the column's comparator or the grid's default order (numbers by value, text ignoring case). Models that sort somewhere else, such as in a database, can ignore it.
      Returns:
      true if the model sorted its rows
